label: a1-vs-a2 choice axis plus rare-transition sign at D2, raised after no reward
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * choice ;; (phase == GO) * choice ;; (phase == D2) * choice ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_common == 0) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1})
explanation: Raw reset gate r46 has a strong timing profile (high at D2, low at GO, decaying over the episode; timing R^2 0.81). Beyond timing it is signed by action: higher when the agent leans or chooses a1, lower for a2. The largest effect is at D2 after a rare transition: a1->S2 raises it by about +0.16 and a2->S1 lowers it by about -0.18 (common transitions are near baseline). The policy logit (a1 minus a2) is a graded term at every phase, strongest at D1. Not being rewarded on the previous trial raises it at GO (+0.05) and D2 (+0.06). At D1, a rare transition on the previous trial carries over with the same sign (a1 S2 up, a2 S1 down, about +-0.05). Value, hidden good state and trials since reversal add little. The terms use only observed inputs and the model policy, with no future variables. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.88 (dev 0.88), against an all ceiling of 0.93 and an all-observed table score of 0.84. Without the policy logit (observed tables only) the score was about 0.52-0.63.

issues: Minor wording issue: the label says the policy-logit term is 'strongest at D1'. That is true of the fitted weights per unit logit (D1 +0.019, GO +0.007, D2 +0.010). By variance it is wrong: dropping the GO choice term cuts test R^2 from 0.879 to 0.634, while dropping the D1 term gives 0.759 and the D2 term 0.740. The logit's range is largest at GO.
The test R^2 of 0.879 reproduces (timing only 0.814). Every term is needed: leave-one-out test R^2 runs from 0.634 to 0.863, and the D2 a1->S2 term is the weakest at 0.863.

The weights back the claims: D2 a1->S2 +0.160 and a2->S1 -0.180; profile D2 residuals are near zero for common transitions (+0.017, +0.006); unrewarded previous trial +0.049 at GO and +0.064 at D2; previous rare transition at D1 +0.052 with action sign.

Misses show no large systematic error class. Mean error by phase is at most 0.008. The largest bias by phase x previous trial is D1 after a1 S2 r at +0.066: the D1 rare carry-over is a bit larger when that rare trial was rewarded, which the symmetric term misses. The others are under 0.03.

Some worst-fit dev windows show GO under-predicted by about 0.15-0.3 for a2 choices after runs of unrewarded trials. None of my tests captured it: a two-loss streak scores 0.884 (+0.005), |choice| or policy-uncertainty at GO scores 0.852-0.866 (worse), and (1 - value) scores 0.878. So it looks idiosyncratic, not a systematic class.

The policy logit is a model output, not an observed input. The label says so and gives the weaker observed-only attempts (0.46-0.63 dev against an all-observed reference of 0.84). That disclosure is adequate, but the observed-only story is clearly less complete.
